name: Benign Focal Seizures of Adolescence
aliases: Benign Childhood Epilepsy with Centrotemporal Spikes

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ILAE Classification of Epilepsies and Epileptic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of focal seizures characterized by unilateral facial sensorimotor symptoms, often involving the oropharyngeal region
EEG demonstrating centrotemporal spikes, typically activated during sleep
Onset of seizures between ages 3 and 13 years with spontaneous remission by adolescence
Normal neurological examination and cognitive development
No structural brain abnormalities on neuroimaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical seizure pattern, EEG findings, and age of onset) must be met for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by EEG; neuroimaging is typically normal and used to exclude other causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral facial sensorimotor seizures involving oropharyngeal muscles
pathognomonic.notes: Typically brief and occur during sleep or drowsiness
searchTerms: one-sided facial and throat muscle seizures
unilateral face and mouth twitching seizures
seizures affecting one side of face and throat
spike patterns in central-temporal brain waves
abnormal EEG spikes near temple area
sharp EEG activity in centrotemporal region

common.symptomName: Tonic-clonic seizures secondary to focal onset
searchTerms: seizures starting in one brain area then spreading
focal onset seizures progressing to convulsions

common.symptomName: Speech arrest or dysarthria during seizures
searchTerms: speech stops or becomes slurred during seizures
speech arrest or unclear speech in seizures

occasional.symptomName: Unilateral clonic jerking of the face or arm
searchTerms: one-sided rhythmic jerking of face or arm
unilateral clonic movements in face or arm
jerking on one side of face or limb
temporary numbness on one side of face
brief tingling or numb face on one side

rare.notes: Extremely rare in this benign syndrome
Rare and usually indicates alternative diagnosis

imaging: Normal brain MRI or CT scan
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; familial aggregation reported in some cases
other: EEG with centrotemporal spikes activated by sleep

distinguishingFeatures: Myoclonic jerks predominantly in the morning
Lifelong epilepsy with no spontaneous remission
Complex partial seizures with impaired awareness
MRI may show mesial temporal sclerosis

redFlags: Seizure onset outside typical age range (before 3 or after 13 years)
Focal neurological deficits or abnormal neuroimaging
references: Orphanet Report on Benign Focal Seizures of Adolescence, ORPHA:1544
